knowledge_point.title: Constructing and Solving a Dilution Model

question.:question/problem:
An aquarium initially holds $480L$ of water containing $13kg$ of dissolved minerals.
A solution containing $0.05kg/L$ of dissolved minerals is pumped into the aquarium at a rate of $24L/min$, while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $36L/min$. If the amount of minerals $Q(t)$, in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by
$Q(t) = α(1 - \frac{t}{40}) + β(1 - \frac{t}{40})^{3}$
where $α$ and $β$ are constants, what is the value of $α + β$?

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution: At $t=0,$ the supplied model gives $Q(0)=\alpha(1-0/40)+\beta(1-0/40)^{3}=\alpha+\beta.$ The initial amount is $13\,\text{kg},$ so $\alpha+\beta=13.$

A solution containing $0.05kg/L$ of dissolved minerals is pumped into the aquarium at a rate of $24L/min$, while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $36L/min$. If the amount of minerals $Q(t)$, in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by
$Q(t) = α(1 - \frac{t}{80}) + β(1 - \frac{t}{80})^{3}$
where $α$ and $β$ are constants, what is the value of $α + β$?

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
question.:question/worked-solution: At $t=0,$ the supplied model gives $Q(0)=\alpha(1-0/80)+\beta(1-0/80)^{3}=\alpha+\beta.$ The initial amount is $11\,\text{kg},$ so $\alpha+\beta=11.$
